rv.q: When the exuberant cast and band are performing Michael Thurber's fabulous score—a seductive blend of Afrobeat, Taarab, R&B, soul and jazz that reflects Kenya's multicultural makeup—the show soars to the skies.
As director, Saheem Ali has created a world seldom seen on the New York stage.
This production is a visual feast.
In this obvious labor of love, Ali’s direction makes us feel the passion and heat generated by the music and dancing at the Moto Moto club.
Its greatest triumph lies in its ability to create moments of pure joy—those electrifying instances when the music, movement, and narrative fuse into something greater than the sum of their parts.
Weaving the Kenyan legend of the goddess of music with a modern-day love story, Goddess bursts onto the stage at The Public Theater with an explosion of joy.
She is now starring in a musical that might do for her what “Touch of Venus” did for Melissa Errico when she portrayed that goddess three decades ago: convert an entire theater into worshippers.
It's impossible to have a bad time at Goddess .
The Public Theater has crafted an unforgettable and utterly unmissable experiences that is satisfying and gratifying in every way.
If your suspension of disbelief is well-honed, Goddess is captivating.
In its current form, it still offers an evening of foot-tapping pleasures and showmanship — and a memorable star turn for the celestial body that is Amber Iman.
The Public Theater production is a grand assemblage of first-rate talent.

cn.t: Critics celebrate this vibrant musical inspired by African mythology, praising Amber Iman's divine performance as the goddess Marimba and the show's electrifying energy, original storytelling, and visually captivating production at the Public Theater.
